recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core source edit is needed unless the work group later decides to prescribe a specific authorization policy for read/vread, which FHIR-8165 explicitly did not do.
issue_request: FHIR-8165 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core HTTP change request asking for explicit authorization caveats around read/vread, including consent and Provenance considerations. The accepted modification was to add general security guidance that operations are subject to RBAC/ABAC, consent, and related access-control decisions rather than prescribing operation-specific policy.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly names FHIR-8165, but the Jira comment says it was applied on 2015-08-21. The matching historical application is commit ae3042ca1e07b476a53c38836836edbf5255a3a2, committed the same day as SVN revision 6464 for the same authorization-qualifier family, which added the REST API security paragraph about authentication, RBAC/ABAC, and consent.
additional_context: Current source keeps the intended general rule in the active RESTful API page and links to the Security page. The Security page now gives broader Authorization/Access Control guidance covering holder authorization, RBAC, ABAC, consent-policy inputs, redaction on read/search, evaluation of all REST access methods, AuditEvent records, and Consent/Provenance examples. A later FHIR-40957 reconciliation changed the wording from 'operations' to 'interactions' but preserved the substance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding a vread-specific rule would be more prescriptive than the Jira resolution allowed and would duplicate maintained security guidance.
